recommendation.because: It is the only option that satisfies SC-001's stated denominator without either claiming coverage this repo does not have (C) or quietly lowering the bar (B); UNREAD-with-a-named-owner is precisely what FR-016 prescribes, and it converts the cross-repo gap from a silent absence into a loud, attributable one that buildkit can discharge later without re-opening 078.

block: The decisions ledger contains a later row that blanks the answer of an already-answered ruling, so a last-wins reader silently loses your decision

options.label: First-answered wins, plus a fold guard

block: Executing the ruled board partition turned up three facts that were not in Q-GLPNETS14-06's evidence, and the first of them makes "similar size" uncomputable as things stand

The scheduler has a verb for the real fix - `effort-assign`, 'declare a story size for one roadmap slot whose effort text names none'.

The roadmap DOES carry effort text for most of them, in four different vocabularies: S/M/L/XL (17 M, 11 L, 4 S, 1 XL), small/medium/large (11 large, 10 medium), M-L and S-M (6), the standard scale itself (2 midi) - and 35 of 120 features carry no effort text at all.

Allocating to an actor whose capabilities are undeclared is how work gets stranded, which the dispatcher is specifically built never to do.

🔴 The cycle now reports dominant_gate=CAPACITY (gate_counts capacity 111, claim-binding 4) with 23 of 25 ready packets deferred. options.label: Partition now over 5 on assumed mini sizes
options.consequence: Executes your instruction immediately across all five calendared actors, including gavri. Fast, but every bundle is balanced on a number I invented, and gavri receives packets whose capability fit is unevaluable. Allocate ops are grow-only on a board five hosts share, so writing 23 of them forecloses this lane's ability to withdraw or re-balance them: only each named assignee can reject its own packets afterwards, and it forecloses ever knowing what the real sizes were, because the assumed mini becomes the board's record.

options.label: Publish the proposal, write no allocate at all
options.consequence: The derived sizes and the proposed partition go to COOP for peer confirmation and nothing is written to the board. Nothing can be got wrong, and nothing moves either - peers have not answered this lane on the last two asks, and the 23 packets stay undispatched.

recommendation.because: It is the only option that makes 'similar size' a measured property rather than a decoration: `effort-assign` turns each size into a declared, auditable board fact, and the roadmap already holds the evidence for all but a handful. Restricting to the four fully-onboarded actors costs one actor's share and removes the one way this write could strand work; B commits 23 irreversible cross-host writes on invented numbers, and C leaves your instruction unexecuted while the board stays exactly as stuck as it is.

decision.rationale: Derive story sizes from roadmap effort text, declare each with effort-assign so the size is a board fact not an assumption, then partition over the four actors with both a calendar and a caps report; gavri is named in the COOP request as needing a caps report first
